sections.title: 2.1 Lične zamenice (Personal Pronouns)
sections.explanation: Lične zamenice označavaju osobe, životinje ili stvari bez ponavljanja imena. Subjekatske zamenice: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Obrazac: SUBJEKAT + GLAGOL + DOPUNA (I am Emma. She is Sophie. They are students.)
rules: I koristimo kada govorimo o sebi – uvek velikim slovom.
You = jedna osoba ili grupa (ti i vi).
He/she za osobe: Oliver → he; Sophie → she.
It za predmet ili pojavu: It is a book.
We = govornik + bar još jedna osoba: Emma and I → we.
They = više osoba ili stvari; može i za jednu osobu nepoznatog roda.
sections.compare: U srpskom se zamenica često izostavlja („Emma sam“), ali u engleskoj izjavi mora da stoji: “I am Emma”, ne “Am Emma”. You pokriva i ti i vi. Pridevi nemaju rod: He is happy. / She is happy.
mistakes: U potpunoj izjavi potreban je subjekat.
I se uvek piše velikim slovom.
sections.remember: I – govornik; you – sagovornik; he/she/it – treće lice jednine; we – govornik i drugi; they – drugi ljudi ili stvari.

sections.title: 2.2 Glagol to be – potvrdni oblik
sections.explanation: To be = „biti“. Koristi se za predstavljanje, ulogu, stanje, opis i mesto. Oblici: am, is, are. Obrazac: SUBJEKAT + AM / IS / ARE + DOPUNA.
rules: Uloga: Ms Taylor is a teacher.
Mesto: We are in the classroom.
Skraćeni oblici su česti u razgovoru; you're (= you are) ≠ your (= tvoj).
sections.compare: Srpski ima sam, si, je, smo, ste, su; engleski samo am, is, are. Uz zanimanje u jednini ide član: “She is a teacher”. Ne kažemo “I am study English” – kažemo “I study English”.
sections.remember: I → am; he / she / it → is; you / we / they → are.

sections.title: 2.3 Neodređeni članovi a / an
sections.explanation: A / AN + IMENICA U JEDNINI. A ispred suglasničkog glasa (a student, a teacher), AN ispred samoglasničkog glasa (an apple, an English teacher). Odlučuje IZGOVOR: a university student, an hour.
rules: Neodređena osoba/stvar: This is a notebook.
Uloga ili zanimanje: Emma is a student.
Prvo uvođenje predmeta: Emma has a notebook.
Pridev + imenica: Sophie is a new student.
NE uz množinu (students), nebrojive imenice (water), imena (I am Emma) ni uz my/your (my notebook).
sections.compare: Srpski nema članove, pa početnici kažu “I am student”. Pravilno je “I am a student”. Izbor a/an nije pitanje roda, već početnog glasa.
mistakes: Uz ulogu u jednini ide član.
sections.remember: Izgovor odlučuje između a i an.

sections.title: 2.4 Korisna pitanja iz dijaloga
sections.explanation: What's your name? – Kako se zoveš? | How are you? – Kako si? | Are you a student? – Da li si polaznik? | How do you spell it? – Kako se slovka? Zasad ih učimo kao gotove fraze; građenje pitanja i negacija slede u lekciji 2.

sections.title: 2.5 Grammar Snapshot
sections.explanation: 1) Zamenice: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. 2) To be: I am / he, she, it is / you, we, they are. 3) a + suglasnički glas, an + samoglasnički glas. 4) Pravimo kratke, tačne potvrdne rečenice.

culture.title: Greetings in English-speaking communities
culture.body:
English is spoken in many parts of the world. People use it at school, at work and when they travel. In English, there are different ways to greet someone. You can say “Hello”, “Hi” or “Good morning”. “Hi” is usually informal. “Good morning” is useful in more formal situations too.

When people say “How are you?”, a short polite answer such as “I'm fine, thanks” is common. Customs vary between people, places and situations. English is not the culture of only one country.
culture.note: Pozdravi zavise od sagovornika, odnosa i konteksta. Ne predstavljamo jednu naviku kao pravilo za sve govornike engleskog.
